question: A 17-year-old boy presents to the clinic with complaints of acne on the trunk and arms. Examination shows multiple sinuses, nodules, and cysts. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following can reduce the risk of sudden cardiac death in a patient with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?

A 40-year-old patient with history of chronic liver disease secondary to hepatitis C, presents to the office with worsening abdominal distention and a new-onset fever. Physical examination reveals massive ascites and deeply jaundiced skin. Paracentesis reveals an absolute neutrophil count of 300/mm3. What is the best treatment option for this patient's condition?
Which one of these is an autosomal recessive condition?

A 45-year-old male patient presents with fatigue, abdominal pain, and jaundice. He is diagnosed with hepatitis and a subsequent hepatoma. He does not have thrombosis or portal hypertension. His MELD score is 12. Which of the following treatment options would be most appropriate?

A patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. The pain is located in the upper right quadrant and is worsened by deep inspiration or movement. The patient has a history of gallstones. What is the initial diagnostic step that should be taken in the evaluation of this patient?

A patient presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain and vomiting. Upon examination, the patient is found to have multiple gallstones and a dilated common bile duct. Laboratory tests reveal a raised serum amylase of 304. What is the most appropriate management for this patient?
A 55-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of chest pain. An ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, avF, V4, V5, and V6. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following drugs is NOT known to cause asthma?
What medication should be avoided in a patient with both asthma and angina?
Which of these drugs can cause hypokalemia?

A 21-year-old male presents with large, painful, deep-seated pimples that are interconnected in multiple areas and often leave scars. They are most predominant on the chest, back, buttocks, and thighs and have grown gradually over the last couple of years. What is the correct diagnosis?

A patient presents with a sudden onset of red, raised, round or oval patches with blisters on her skin after taking a new medication for a respiratory infection. The patches are symmetrical and are accompanied by fever, malaise, and mouth sores. What is the correct diagnosis?

A 30-year-old male presents with thick, red, scaly patches on their scalp, elbows, and knees. They have had these patches for several years and they have not responded to over-the-counter creams. The patches are itchy and sometimes bleed when scratched. What is the appropriate initial treatment option?

A 29-year-old female presents with a sudden onset of a red, painful rash on their chest, arms, and legs. The rash has evolved into blisters and ulcers, and the affected body surface area is less than 10%. The patient is also experiencing fever, sore throat, and conjunctivitis. What is the correct diagnosis?

A patient with a history of chronic hepatitis B presents with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. They are found to have ascites but no jaundice. Further testing reveals elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin. What is the correct diagnosis?

A 65-year-old man presents to the emergency department with sudden onset of chest pain radiating to his left arm. He is diaphoretic and short of breath. An ECG shows ST-segment elevation in the lateral leads. The patient is diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction involving the lateral wall. What is the most appropriate 'initial' management for this patient?

A 50-year-old male with liver cirrhosis develops fever with chills, diffuse abdominal pain, constipation, and confusion. His laboratory reports from 3 days ago showed increased prothrombin time, AST and ALT, and bilirubin. An ultrasound-guided paracentesis is carried out, and peritoneal fluid analysis showed a neutrophil count of 300 x 10^6/L. Bacterial cultures from the peritoneal fluid are awaited. 

Which of the following the best option for the treatment of this patient?

A 34-year-old female presents to the clinic with the complaint of a rash on her skin. The rash was initially only an erythematous macule, which then progressed to become papular and vesicular lesions. Currently, the lesions appear concentric with an inner erythematosus zone, surrounded by a pale zone and an outer erythematous ring. The rash started on the dorsal aspect of both her hands and has progressively spread to involve her arms and trunk. The patient has a past medical history of a UTI 3 weeks back which was treated with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. 

Which of the following is most likely the diagnosis?

A 34-year-old patient is brought to the emergency room with complaints of jaundice and aggressiveness for 4 days.  Her husband found an empty container of paracetamol 8 days ago. 
What is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

answers.option: Acute decompensation of chronic liver disease

question:
A 58-year-old woman presents to the outpatient department for a general health checkup. Her blood pressure is 140/100 mm Hg, and her pulse rate is 89 per minute. The rest of her vitals are normal. She is 163 cm tall (5'4") and weighs 102 kg (225 lbs). Her BMI is 38.4 kg/m². She mentions that she frequently wakes up from her sleep and her husband constantly complains about her snoring. 
The physician advises her to lose weight for better health, but the patient complains that she has tried multiple times and follows the advice of her nutritionist religiously. She mentions she has heard of bariatric surgery and has been considering it for some time. 
The physician advises trying medical therapy before moving on to surgical intervention. 

Which of the following medications is usually prescribed to help weight loss only?

A 63-year-old patient with chronic hepatitis B was brought to the emergency room in a state of confusion and drowsiness. Four days ago he developed constipation, which has not been relieved. On inspection, he is jaundiced and has abdominal distension. 

Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment option for this patient?

A 30-year-old woman is being treated for inflammatory bowel disease. The physician is considering adding infliximab to her treatment plan. Coexistence of which of the following diseases is a contraindication to the prescription of infliximab?

A 55-year-old patient who is being treated for pneumonia experiences worsening shortness of breath. Arterial blood gas analysis shows pH = 7.37, PaO2= 55 mmHg, PaCO2 = 30 mmHg, and HCO3= 25 mEq/L. 
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

answers.option: Acute on chronic type II respiratory failure

question: A patient with COPD experiences worsening dyspnea and increased frequency and severity of his cough. He is given inhaled ipratropium and albuterol to provide relief. The physician is suspecting acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD). Which of the following is the next best step to establish a diagnosis?

answers.option: Pulmonary function testing (PFT) before and after bronchodilator

question:
The modified Duke's criteria are used to classify the probability of infective endocarditis  (IE) as definitive or possible.  
The diagnosis of definitive IE according to Duke's criteria is made when which of the following options is fulfilled?
Which of the following is the most common cause of dizziness in patients younger than 65 years?
Which of the following is the most common cause of syncope in the general population?

A 53-year-old female presents to the clinic with progressive abdominal distention and dyspnea.  On examination, there was shifting dullness. An abdominal ultrasound is carried out to confirm the accumulation of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity. Diagnostic paracentesis is then carried out and analysis of ascitic fluid shows serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) =  1.4 g/dL. 

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

A 40-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of fatigue, muscle weakness, Raynaud's phenomenon, and polyarthritis. Further workup reveals raised anti-SSA and anti-SSB antibodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
Which of the following is the most common cause of bronchiectasis worldwide?

A 36-year-old male, who is a refugee presents to the clinic with complaints of chronic cough and weight loss. Chest X-ray shows patchy opacification of the middle lobes.  Sputum culture shows the presence of acid-fast bacilli. He has no comorbidites. He is started on anti-tuberculous therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate combination and duration of treatment?

answers.option: 12 months of rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol
2 months of rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, and 4 months of rifampin and isoniazid.
4 months of rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, and 2 months of rifampin and isoniazid.

question:
A 35 year-old-female presents to the ER with complaints of blurry vision, loss of central vision, and retrobulbar pain triggered by eye movements. 
Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's signs and symptoms?

A 23-year-old female, with a past medical history of bulimia nervosa, presents to the clinic with complaints of recurrent abdominal pain, bloating, and altered bowel habits, interchanging between diarrhea and constipation. After a thorough history, examinations, and exclusion of other diseases, the physician eventually diagnoses this patient with irritable bowel syndrome. 
Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment plan for this patient's pain and bloating?

answers.option: Reassurance, dietary changes and spasmolytic drugs

question:
A 30-year-old male presents to the clinic with complaints of a fever of 103°F (39.4 °C)  with rigors and chills, dyspnea, and a productive cough. 
On examination, the patient has a respiratory rate of 21 breaths per minute and thoracic retractions. On auscultation, crackles and decreased breath sounds can be heard in the right upper lobe. 
The physician makes a provisional clinical diagnosis of lobar pneumonia. Which of the following is the next best investigation?

answers.option: Sputum gram staining, culture and antimicrobial sensitivity testing

question:
A 64-year-old male with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy and a previous history of MI presents to the clinic with a complaint of recurrent syncope. Echocardiogram shows an increase in left ventricular wall thickness from last year. 
Which of the following is the most suitable option to prevent sudden cardiac death in this patient?
Which of the following is the most common cause of sudden cardiac death?
Which of the following is most appropriate for the treatment of bradycardia?

A 9-year-old boy is being evaluated for his gait abnormality and abdominal pain. Upon further assessment, he has hepatosplenomegaly and portal hypertension. His physicians are suspecting Wilson's disease and order blood and urine tests, accordingly. Which of the following combinations are his physicians expecting to see on his laboratory reports?

answers.option: High urinary copper, low serum ceruloplasmin, high hepatic copper.
Low urinary copper, high serum ceruloplasmin, high hepatic copper.
High urinary copper, high serum ceruloplasmin, high hepatic copper.
High urinary copper, high serum ceruloplasmin, high hepatic copper, low free copper
High urinary copper, low serum ceruloplasmin, high hepatic copper, low free copper

question: A patient presents to the ER with a fever, associated with chills and rigors. X-ray shows an elevated right hemidiaphragm and effusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 60-year-old male presents to the clinic with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, associated with high-grade fever, nausea, and vomiting. A provisional diagnosis of acute pancreatitis is made and physicians are fearing complications. Which of the following is NOT a complication of acute pancreatitis?
Klinefelter syndrome is due to which of the following chromosomal abnormalities?

A 17-year-old male presents to the clinic with concerns about gynecomastia. He is a tall, slim boy with long extremities. On examination, he has reduced facial and body hair, and small external genitalia. 

Which of the following is most likely the underlying cause of this condition?

A 17-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with several painful nodular and ulcerating lesions on his trunk along with fever and arthralgias for the past 2 days. He has a history of cystic acne for the past 2 years. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 45-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with a widespread rash involving her hands and feet that she noticed one day ago. She also has had low-grade fever and malaise for the past 5 days. Two weeks ago, she was diagnosed with a urinary tract infection and prescribed nitrofurantoin. On examination, several tender, erythematous and blistering lesions are noted on her limbs and face, involving less than 10% of the total body surface along with oral ulcers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
